analysis.summary: Nisha Reddy left for clearer growth opportunities, finding the SDR role's targets unrealistic and progression unclear, despite appreciating the team environment and initial learning. She noted a prevalent issue within the Sales Development team regarding aggressive targets and insufficient leadership support.

key_themes.evidence: unrealistic call/quota targets and little visibility into how to actually get promoted; career conversations never really happened.
unrealistic call/quota targets; pressure is relentless; aggressive targets without enough lead support.

leadership sets aggressive targets without enough lead support; Feedback in pipeline reviews felt more like criticism than coaching; One-on-ones were often cancelled; activity-metric focus felt demotivating.
Great onboarding buddy and a friendly SDR pod.
learned a lot about outbound in a short time and the tooling (Salesforce) was solid.

recommendations.action: Review and adjust sales targets/quotas for SDRs to be more realistic.
Provide more leadership support and coaching to the SDR team, focusing on constructive feedback over criticism.
Support managers (e.g., Karan) to ensure they have capacity for regular 1:1s and career development discussions.
Address the 'activity-metric focus' to improve team motivation.

reasons_for_leaving: Received an offer with clearer growth opportunities.
SDR role felt like a treadmill due to unrealistic targets and lack of promotion visibility.
